eval_instructions: Test against agents that are NOT yet M365-integrated across three languages: Node.js (LangChain/OpenAI/Claude), .NET AgentFramework, and Python AgentFramework. The skill must WRAP existing LLM code, not replace it. For Node.js verify: (1) index.ts has CloudAdapter + authorizeJWT + /api/health + /api/messages, (2) agent.ts has AgentApplication with message/notification/InstallationUpdate handlers + side-effect import of @microsoft/agents-a365-notifications, (3) client.ts has getClient() factory wrapping existing LLM — NO ObservabilityManager/McpToolRegistrationService here, (4) token-cache.ts exists with createAgenticTokenCacheKey, (5) only @microsoft/agents-hosting and @microsoft/agents-a365-notifications packages added (NOT tooling/observability), (6) tsconfig has module: node16. For .NET verify: (1) Program.cs has AddAgent<T> + /api/messages + /api/health — NO AddAgenticTracingExporter/AddA365Tracing/IMcpToolRegistrationService, (2) agent class extends AgentApplication with dual isAgenticOnly registrations + GetClientAgent(), (3) .csproj has Microsoft.Agents.A365.Notifications and Microsoft.Agents.Hosting.AspNetCore, (4) appsettings.json has AgentApplication + TokenValidation. For Python verify: (1) host_agent_server.py has CloudAdapterAiohttp + /api/messages + /api/health + on_agent_notification, (2) agent.py implements AgentInterface with process_user_message + _sanitize_display_name + token_resolver, (3) token_cache.py exists, (4) pyproject.toml has microsoft_agents_a365_notifications + microsoft_agents_a365_runtime + microsoft-agents-hosting-aiohttp (NOT tooling/observability). Phase 9: a365.config.json with full naming fields, a365 config init, dry-run shown + confirmed, a365 setup all. Phase 10: manifest/manifest.json review, a365 publish, Teams Dev Portal (a365 config display --field agentBlueprintId). Phase 11: Observability offered (Strongly Recommended). Phase 12: WorkIQ offered (Optional, OBO note). Phase 13: Local testing offered. Phase 14: Final summary.

evals.prompt: Make this agent an AI Teammate
evals.description: Full transformation of a plain Node.js LangChain script with no M365 integration
evals.expected_output: The skill detects LangChain, confirms with the user, installs @microsoft/agents-hosting and @microsoft/agents-a365-notifications, writes src/index.ts with CloudAdapter + JWT auth + health + messages endpoints, writes src/agent.ts with AgentApplication + all handlers + side-effect notification import, writes src/client.ts with getClient() factory wrapping existing LangChain invocation, writes src/token-cache.ts, updates .env.example with A365 variables, updates tsconfig.json to node16, validates the build, then walks through Phase 9 (config + setup), Phase 10 (publish + Teams Dev Portal), Phase 11 (observability offer), Phase 12 (WorkIQ offer), Phase 13 (local test offer), Phase 14 (final summary).
expectations: Phase 0A: language detected as NodeJS from package.json
Phase 0A: LangChain is detected from package.json
Phase 0A: hasHosting, hasAgentApp, hasClientFactory, hasTokenCache are all detected as ❌
Phase 0B: Detection summary shown to user with 'already present' flags all ❌
Phase 0B: User is asked to confirm before any files are written
Phase 1: npm install runs with @microsoft/agents-hosting and @microsoft/agents-a365-notifications — NOT observability or tooling packages
Phase 2: tsconfig.json has module: node16 and moduleResolution: node16
Phase 3: src/token-cache.ts is created with createAgenticTokenCacheKey, tokenResolver, and default export
Phase 4: src/index.ts has configDotenv() as first line before other imports
Phase 4: src/index.ts has /api/health BEFORE authorizeJWT middleware
Phase 4: src/index.ts has /api/messages using adapter.process()
Phase 4: src/index.ts detects production via WEBSITE_SITE_NAME or NODE_ENV=production
Phase 5: src/agent.ts exports agentApplication as a named const
Phase 5: src/agent.ts has onAgentNotification('agents:*') with priority 1 and [authHandlerName]
Phase 5: src/agent.ts has onActivity(ActivityTypes.Message) with [authHandlerName]
Phase 5: src/agent.ts has onActivity(ActivityTypes.InstallationUpdate)
Phase 5: src/agent.ts has typing indicator loop (setInterval every 4000ms)
Phase 5: src/agent.ts imports '@microsoft/agents-a365-notifications' as side-effect (no ObservabilityManager or McpToolRegistrationService)
Phase 5: src/agent.ts uses createEmailResponseActivity for email replies
Phase 6: src/client.ts has getClient() factory function wrapping the existing LangChain invocation
Phase 6: src/client.ts uses createAgenticTokenCacheKey for token cache key management
Phase 6: src/client.ts does NOT import ObservabilityManager, McpToolRegistrationService, or InferenceScope
Phase 7: .env.example gains agentic_* vars, BEARER_TOKEN, PORT=3978, connection vars
Phase 8: npm run build (or tsc --noEmit) succeeds
Phase 9: User is asked for Agent Name and Manager Email in a single message
Phase 9: User is asked whether to use devtunnel or custom endpoint for Messaging Endpoint
Phase 9: a365.config.json is created with tenantId, full naming fields (agentIdentityDisplayName, agentUserPrincipalName, etc.), and messagingEndpoint
Phase 9: a365 config init -c ./a365.config.json is run to import the config
Phase 9: a365 setup all --dry-run output is shown to user for confirmation before running
Phase 9: a365 setup all runs and creates the Blueprint with Agentic User UPN and permissions
Phase 9: Admin consent action item (Permission Grants) is shown to user if present in output
Phase 10: manifest/manifest.json fields are reviewed and user confirms all are filled before publishing
Phase 10: a365 publish runs to publish manifest to M365 Admin Center
Phase 10: Teams Developer Portal steps are provided using 'a365 config display -g --field agentBlueprintId' to get the URL
Phase 10: Teams > Apps > Request Instance steps are explained (not CLI create-instance)
Phase 11: User is asked separately: 'Would you like to add observability now?' (strongly recommended)
Phase 12: User is asked separately: 'Would you like to add WorkIQ tools?' with OBO token consent note
Phase 13: User is asked whether to test locally with AgentsPlayground
Phase 14: Final summary shows hosting layer, agent class, client factory, token cache, A365 registered, published status
